sourcesRead.what: Full public in-app What's New changelog, builds 136–463 (2026-04-23 → 2026-10-08), read from src/data/changelog.ts on origin/main (entries restricted via visibleTo excluded); 'new' sections read in full, 'improved'/'fixed' scanned for capabilities and removals
Roadmap — SHIPPED section and 'Under the hood' used; 'Coming next' and the competitor matrix ignored

claims.detail: Log sets, reps and weight for lifts.
claims.quote: Log lifts, cardio, sleep, food, weight, and habits in seconds.

claims.detail: Weight and reps shown large with one tap per set to check it off.
claims.quote: Big numbers. One tap a set.

claims.detail: In-workout keyboard built for entering weight and reps instead of the system keyboard.
claims.quote: A new in-workout keyboard built for lifting: type your weight and reps without the system keyboard getting in the way, jump straight from weight to reps, and tap to complete a set.

claims.feature: One movement open at a time
claims.detail: Live workout focuses on the current movement; others collapse to one line.
claims.quote: The movement you're on gets the screen. Everything else folds to a line with its rest and its progress. Open one, the others close.

claims.detail: Weight fields start filled with what was lifted last time, configurable per movement.
claims.quote: Your weight fields can start already filled in with what you lifted last time. Templates do it by default; a quick start stays empty unless you turn it on

claims.detail: Group movements to be logged back-to-back, round by round.
claims.quote: Supersets and giant sets: group exercises so they’re logged back-to-back.

claims.detail: Group three or more movements together.
claims.quote: Supersets and giant sets: group exercises so they’re logged back-to-back.

claims.detail: Build circuits of segments with auto-advancing timers.
claims.quote: Same circuit editor covers HIIT, Tabata, and boot-camp-style sequences — reach it from the round-config sheet via "Or build a circuit"

claims.detail: Turn a set into a drop set with lighter efforts logged beneath it.
claims.quote: Drop sets: turn any set into a drop set — strip the weight and keep going, with the lighter efforts logged right beneath it.

claims.detail: Set the default percentage a drop set reduces weight by.
claims.quote: Drop set reduction, from 5% to 60%.

claims.detail: Tag sets as warm-ups, kept out of records.
claims.quote: Warm-ups stop polluting your records, failure sets explain themselves, and drops and partials get lines of their own under the set they belong to.

claims.detail: Tag sets as taken to failure.
claims.quote: Warm-up and failure sets: tag any set as a warm-up or a to-failure set from the set menu. They’re color-coded everywhere you see them.

claims.detail: Tag a set as a top set.
claims.quote: Tap a set's number: warm-up, regular, top set, failure, a drop set — or partials.

claims.detail: Log half-range reps after a set; counted toward volume at half a rep each.
claims.quote: Partials. Finished a set with half reps to failure? Add partials from the set’s menu, or just say it

claims.detail: Set different reps per set (pyramids, dropsets) in templates and plans.
claims.quote: Set per-set reps on templates and planned workouts — dropsets like 10/8/6 or pyramids like 5/5/3 are now first-class

claims.detail: Log reps left in the tank per set via an effort slider.
claims.quote: Log how many reps you had left in the tank (reps in reserve) with the Effort slider

claims.detail: Rate the effort of a session on phone or watch.
claims.quote: Rate your effort on the watch using the same four-band chart as the phone, and drag across it to pick instead of tapping.

claims.detail: Shows which plates to load for a weight, or computes weight from tapped plates.
claims.quote: Tap the bar to see which plates to load, or tap plates to get the weight.

claims.detail: Choose grip, width and handle attachment per movement or per set.
claims.quote: Handles: wide lat bar, straight bar, EZ bar, V-handle, wide neutral handle, rope, single handle.

claims.detail: History, records and last-time weights tracked separately per grip.
claims.quote: Last time’s weights follow the grip you picked — and one set can have a different grip from the rest.

claims.detail: Swap a movement and closest alternatives (same pattern, different equipment) are listed first.
claims.quote: Switch it, and SPLYT lists the closest alternatives first — same movement pattern, same muscles, and deliberately a different piece of equipment

claims.detail: Leave a note on a movement that shows next time.
claims.quote: Leave yourself a note, and it's on the card next time.

claims.feature: Copy sets from a past session
claims.detail: Paste a past session's sets onto the current movement.
claims.quote: Use these sets — paste the sets from a past session straight onto the movement you are working on.

claims.detail: Fill one movement's weights from another by voice.
claims.quote: Ask for your numbers from another movement — "put my leg curl weights on the leg extension" — and Splyt fills them in.

claims.detail: Drag exercises to reorder during a workout; supersets move as a block.
claims.quote: Workouts — reorder mid-workout with supersets moving as one block

claims.detail: Collapse an exercise card to a single line.
claims.quote: Collapse exercise cards — tap the chevron next to any exercise to shrink it down to a single line showing just the name and set count.

claims.detail: Rename an active workout.
claims.quote: Rename your workout on the fly — tap ⋮ during any active workout and choose "Rename Workout" to give it a custom name.

claims.detail: Set how many sets and reps a new exercise starts with.
claims.quote: Workout Defaults in settings — set how many sets and reps a new exercise starts with (defaults to 3 × 10).

claims.detail: Let a plan record as planned instead of logging every set.
claims.quote: Log every set, or switch a plan to follow-along and let it record as planned.

claims.detail: Track a lift with only a label, time, heart rate and calories, no sets.
claims.quote: Simple Mode for Traditional Strength Training — tap "Simple Mode" at the bottom of the workout sheet, pick what you're hitting today

claims.detail: Bodyweight movements count toward volume using your body weight.
claims.quote: Pull-ups, dips and push-ups finally count toward your volume. A bodyweight movement is scored with your own weight plus anything you added

claims.detail: Unnamed strength sessions are labeled by muscles trained.
claims.quote: Finish a strength workout without naming it and Splyt now labels it by what you trained

claims.detail: Edit or delete any past workout.
claims.quote: You can now edit or delete any of your own past workouts, not just your most recent ones.

claims.detail: Log an activity after the fact with a chosen duration.
claims.quote: When you log an activity by hand, you can now set exactly how long it lasted.

claims.detail: Finish a workout without signal; it syncs when back online.
claims.quote: No signal, no problem — if you finish a workout with no connection, it’s saved on your device and syncs automatically the moment you’re back online.

claims.detail: New PRs are celebrated mid-workout and marked on the set.
claims.quote:
A personal record is a moment now. The rest bar opens into a card showing
how far you beat your best, and the set keeps the trophy.

claims.detail: Log in kg or lb, applied everywhere including past workouts.
claims.quote: Log in kilograms. Pick it once — in Workout Defaults, or from any movement’s ⋯ menu — and everything follows

claims.detail: Swipe mid-workout to see volume/time filling against last, typical and best sessions plus HR and calories vs usual.
claims.quote: A glass fills with the weight you've moved, past your last, your typical and your best — with your heart rate and calories against your usual.

claims.feature: Live heart-rate graph vs last time
claims.detail: Graph of heart rate during session with last session as a ghost line.
claims.quote: Flip it to Graph for your heart rate over time with last time’s as a ghost.

claims.detail: Swipe during a workout to see recent sessions of that activity.
claims.quote: During a live workout, swipe right past your rings to see your recent sessions of that activity — and how long each one was.

claims.detail: Search to start a workout, including saved templates.
claims.quote: Searching to start a workout now finds your saved workouts too.

claims.detail: Banner to jump back into an in-progress session.
claims.quote: A live-workout banner now sits atop the workout picker so you can jump straight back into a session already in progress.

claims.detail: 3-2-1 countdown when starting a workout, mirrored on watch.
claims.quote: Starting a workout now plays a get-ready sequence — the ring fills up, then counts you in 3, 2, 1.

claims.detail: Prompts "Still working out?" when a session seems abandoned.
claims.quote: “Still working out?” is smarter. With your Apple Watch on, your heart rate decides

claims.detail: Rest timer between sets with built-in timers.
claims.quote: Log sets, reps and weight in seconds, with rest timers built right in.

claims.detail: Each movement remembers its own rest duration.
claims.quote: Every movement remembers its own rest — change it right on the card and it sticks, session after session.

claims.detail: Give each set its own rest duration.
claims.quote: Turn on custom rest times and give each set its own — short on warm-ups, long on the heavy compounds.

claims.detail: Drag the rest pill to add or remove 15 seconds.
claims.quote: Drag it right for more time, left for less, fifteen seconds a step.

claims.detail: Phone chimes and vibrates when rest ends; configurable when wearing a watch.
claims.quote: Your phone now chimes and vibrates when a rest timer ends, so you know your set is up without a watch.

claims.detail: Display rest as a line between set rows; tap to edit a single gap.
claims.quote: A new option draws each rest as a line between your set rows, so you can see the whole set-rest-set rhythm at a glance.

claims.detail: Start a rest from the workout dock for any activity.
claims.quote: Live workout dock can start a manual rest from the expanded menu — works for any activity (not just lifting).

claims.detail: Choose whether warm-up sets trigger a rest.
claims.quote: A rest after warm-up sets, or straight on.

claims.detail: Supports over ninety activity types from strength to swimming to recovery.
claims.quote: activity types, from strength to swimming to recovery.

claims.detail: Chain several activities into one session saved as one workout.
claims.quote: Chain a lift, a game and a sauna into one session, saved as one workout.

claims.detail: Timer-driven views for sports like basketball, pickleball, yoga, pilates.
claims.quote: Workouts beyond lifting — tap activities like Basketball, Pickleball, Yoga, or Pilates and you get a clean timer-driven view instead of empty sets and reps

claims.detail: Work/rest rounds with haptics at each transition.
claims.quote: Boxing & martial arts — pre-set work / rest / total rounds and the live view auto-flips between work and rest with a haptic at every transition

claims.detail: Interval circuits for HIIT, Tabata and boot camp.
claims.quote: Same circuit editor covers HIIT, Tabata, and boot-camp-style sequences

claims.detail: Core Training as a template workout type.
claims.quote: Core Training is now one of the workout types when you create a template.

claims.detail: Outdoor runs, walks, rides and hikes tracked by phone GPS with live pace and route map.
claims.quote: Track outdoor workouts with just your phone — no Apple Watch needed. Start an outdoor walk, run, ride, or hike and watch your distance, pace, and route map update live

claims.detail: Outdoor workouts save a route map with heatmap coloring.
claims.quote: Outdoor walks, runs, and rides now save their route map, so when you share a workout your friends see the same map you do — with new heatmap coloring

claims.detail: Workout summary shows elevation gain.
claims.quote: Your workout summary now shows elevation gain, and friends can see it on yours too.

claims.detail: Pick pool length; watch counts laps.
claims.quote: Pool swim — pick your pool length (25 yd, 50 yd, 25 m, 50 m, or custom) and your watch auto-counts laps as you swim

claims.detail: Live total strokes during open water swims.
claims.quote: Total strokes now shows live during open water swims on both your phone and Apple Watch.

claims.detail: Sauna, steam room, jacuzzi, cold plunge, ice bath and massage logged as recovery.
claims.quote: Recovery activities — Sauna, Steam Room, Jacuzzi, Cold Plunge, Ice Bath, Leg Massage, and Back Massage are now in the activity picker on iPhone and Apple Watch

claims.detail: Photograph a cardio machine screen to import distance, calories, time, pace.
claims.quote: Point your camera at a cardio machine’s console and Splyt reads your stats off it — distance, calories, time and pace — then folds them into your workout details.

claims.detail: Mark a day as a rest day, optionally with a session.
claims.quote: A rest day can still carry a session — a swim on your rest day — and it is still a rest day.

claims.detail: Describe a whole day of activities and they become separate workouts.
claims.quote: Tell the voice logger your whole day, not one workout.

claims.detail: Library of 1,513 exercises each with demo, muscles and grips.
claims.quote:
1,513
exercises
Each with a demo, the muscles it works, and the grips and handles it takes.

claims.detail: Every exercise has an animated demo and step-by-step instructions.
claims.quote: Every exercise now has an animated demo and step-by-step instructions on its detail screen

claims.detail: Body diagram highlights primary and supporting muscles of each exercise.
claims.quote: tap an exercise in the picker and a body diagram lights up the primary and supporting muscles.

claims.detail: Create custom exercises with description and instructions.
claims.quote: Custom exercises now have their own how-to — add a description and step-by-step instructions when you create one

claims.detail: AI writes description, how-to, body part and equipment for a custom exercise.
claims.quote: Auto-fill a custom exercise with AI — tap the sparkle when you create or edit one

claims.detail: Send a custom exercise to a friend as their own copy.
claims.quote: Share a custom exercise with a friend in Splyt — they get their own copy, instructions included

claims.detail: Search/filter exercise library from Stats.
claims.quote: Browse the whole exercise library from Stats without starting a workout.

claims.detail: Per-movement history with estimated 1RM, volume, weight over time and PRs.
claims.quote: Tap any movement for its full record: your one-rep max, volume and weight over time, the personal records that matter up front, and every session you've done with it.

claims.detail: Save go-to sessions and start in a tap.
claims.quote: Save your go-to sessions, sort them into folders, and start any one in a tap.

claims.detail: Organize saved workouts into folders; one workout in multiple folders.
claims.quote: Organize your saved workouts into folders — create folders, move workouts in, rename or delete, and search within a folder.

claims.detail: Share a saved-workout folder read-only with friends.
claims.quote: Share a saved-workout folder with friends — they’ll see it (read-only) in their Saved tab

claims.detail: Supersets, drop sets, warm-up/failure sets built into templates.
claims.quote: Build supersets, drop sets, and warm-up/failure sets right into your templates

claims.detail: Sixteen weekly splits and five rotating cycles sorted by days per week.
claims.quote: sixteen weekly splits and five rotating cycles, sorted by how many days a week you can actually train, each with a body map of what it hits.

claims.detail: One tap fills each training day with exercises, sets and reps.
claims.quote: Picked a proven split like Push / Pull / Legs? One tap fills every day with starter exercises — sets and reps included

claims.detail: Splits that cycle (e.g. 4 on, 1 off) independent of weekdays.
claims.quote: Splits can roll instead of repeating on weekdays. Four days on, one off keeps going round whatever day it lands on

claims.detail: Build a weekly split by hand.
claims.quote: tap the grid to pick a proven split, sorted by how many days a week you can train, or build one by hand.

claims.detail: Calendar of planned, completed, missed and rest days.
claims.quote: Plan days ahead and see every completed, missed and rest day, week by week.

claims.detail: Month view with a ring per day.
claims.quote: Zoom out to the month and every day wears its ring

claims.detail: Press and hold a planned workout and move it to another day.
claims.quote: Press and hold a planned workout in the training calendar and carry it to another day.

claims.detail: Copy a planned or trained day onto another day.
claims.quote: Copy a day on your training calendar.

claims.detail: Pin clock times to planned workouts and splits.
claims.quote: Optionally pin a clock time to planned workouts and to a split

claims.detail: Shows the hour you usually train and warns about sleep collisions.
claims.quote: When you pick a time to train, Splyt now tells you the hour you usually train

claims.detail: Unstarted planned workouts show as missed and can be logged late or moved.
claims.quote: Missed a planned workout? It now shows as “Missed” and stays on your record

claims.detail: Edit or cancel recurrences of repeating plans.
claims.quote: for a repeating plan, choose whether it’s just this day or every one from here on.

claims.detail: Planned workouts appear in Apple Calendar.
claims.quote: Your planned workouts appear in Apple Calendar automatically.

claims.detail: Import multiple screenshots as one split.
claims.quote: Your trainer sent screenshots? Pick them all at once and they come in as one split, in order.

claims.detail: See a friend's planned and completed days read-only.
claims.quote: See a friend’s week — their planned and completed days, read-only, from the calendar header.

claims.detail: Send a split to a friend.
claims.quote: Share a split straight from the split itself. Pick a friend and it lands under their From friends.

claims.detail: Template page shows recent runs as a trend.
claims.quote: A template’s graph page shows your last few times doing it

claims.detail: Chat coach that answers from your training history.
claims.quote: Ask why your bench stalled. It answers from your own training — your sessions, your records, your recovery — not the internet.

claims.detail: Coach remembers goals, injuries and routines across conversations.
claims.quote: Splyt AI remembers your goals, injuries, and routines across every conversation.

claims.detail: Coach draws charts from your data.
claims.quote: Splyt AI can draw charts inline now

claims.detail: Coach searches the web for current info and shows sources.
claims.quote: Splyt AI can now search the web live when you ask about something current, and shows you its sources.

claims.detail: Attach a photo to the AI coach; it remembers it later.
claims.quote: You can attach a photo to Splyt AI — a machine you do not recognise, a page from a program, a meal

claims.detail: Continuous searchable conversation.
claims.quote: Splyt AI is now one continuous conversation you can scroll back through — and search across everything you’ve asked.

claims.detail: AI drafts a template you can save or discard.
claims.quote: Splyt AI can draft a single workout template too

claims.detail: AI drafts a full weekly split from goal, days and equipment.
claims.quote: Splyt AI can build entire workout splits for you — answer three quick questions (goal, days per week, equipment)

claims.detail: AI-built workouts include warm-up, top, failure, drop sets and supersets.
claims.quote: Splyt AI now builds real programs — workouts come with warm-up, top, failure, and drop sets and supersets, not just a flat list.

claims.detail: Ask the AI to edit your existing split.
claims.quote: Splyt AI can now edit your existing split — just ask.

claims.detail: Split generation asks about injuries and swaps movements.
claims.quote: Injuries get the movement swapped rather than the day skipped.

claims.detail: AI generates today's session live during a workout.
claims.quote: Splyt AI inside an active workout

claims.detail: Set goals from a sentence; coach tracks and flags unrealistic ones.
claims.quote: Set a goal for any activity just by telling Splyt AI

claims.detail: AI-proposed plans require a Confirm tap before landing on calendar.
claims.quote: Every plan shows you a Confirm card first — nothing lands on your calendar until you tap it.

claims.detail: Weekly AI read on the last 7 days with one-tap actions.
claims.quote: A fresh read on your last week, with one-tap next steps, before the new one starts.

claims.detail: Short plain-language story of the training week, shareable.
claims.quote: Weekly Story: a short, plain-language recap of your training week at the top of your Splyt Coach insights — and you can share it as a card.

claims.detail: Scroll through past weekly insights.
claims.quote: Insight History — tap the clock icon on the Stats Coach widget to scroll through every week's past insights.

claims.detail: Coach shows a movement's card with history and how-to.
claims.quote: Ask the coach about a movement and it shows the movement’s card, with a tap into your history and how to do it.

claims.detail: AI read on physique with annotated callouts.
claims.quote: Progress photo AI analysis (Pro): upload your front, side, and back photos together and get an AI read on your physique, with annotated callouts and a card you can share.

claims.detail: In-app support chat with AI assistant and human team.
claims.quote: Pro members can now chat directly with support from their profile.

claims.detail: Say what you did and sets, weights, set types land on the card.
claims.quote: Plates, quarters, "the bar", "three by three", "to failure" — SPLYT gets the weights, the reps and the set types right, for one movement or five, in a loud gym.

claims.detail: Fix already-logged sets by voice.
claims.quote: Correct sets you have already logged by voice.

claims.detail: Say "superset" to group the current round.
claims.quote: Say "superset" during a workout and Splyt will group the round you are on

claims.detail: Log sets, skip rest, move to next exercise, ask for recommendations by voice.
claims.quote: AI Voice Agent in workouts — log sets, skip rest, move to the next exercise, and ask for exercise recommendations, all by voice.

claims.detail: Build a template by talking, then keep talking to edit it.
claims.quote: Build a workout by talking. Tap the mic while making a template and say what you want

claims.detail: Describe your week out loud and it becomes a split with days and times.
claims.quote: Say your split. Tap the mic in the split builder and describe your week

claims.detail: Tell the app a finished workout and it lands in history.
claims.quote: Voice quick-log a workout you already finished — just tell Splyt what you did and it lands in your history.

claims.detail: Set grips by voice.
claims.quote: Tell the voice logger how you held it

claims.detail: Start, pause, resume or end any activity with Siri on iPhone or Watch.
claims.quote: Start any activity, pause, resume or finish with Siri on iPhone or Apple Watch.

claims.detail: Siri commands work on a locked phone.
claims.quote: Siri on a locked phone

claims.detail: Log full workouts from the wrist with HR and calories.
claims.quote: Log full workouts from your wrist, with heart rate and calories synced to your phone.

claims.detail: Watch counts reps on presses, curls, squats, pulldowns, triceps, flyes.
claims.quote: Your watch counts reps on presses, curls, squats, pulldowns and more — hands-free.

claims.detail: Rep detection runs on-watch without signal.
claims.quote: Runs entirely on-device, so it works with no signal.

claims.detail: Phone shows a giant live rep count while watch counts.
claims.quote: your phone now takes over the whole screen with a giant live count you can read from across the room

claims.detail: Add, delete, adjust sets, swap movements, set grips, start rests from wrist.
claims.quote: Add, delete and adjust sets, swap moves, set grips and start rests from your wrist.

claims.detail: Swap an exercise for a similar one from the watch.
claims.quote: Switch an exercise from your watch.

claims.detail: Wheel pickers with Digital Crown for weight/reps.
claims.quote: use the Digital Crown to dial it in

claims.detail: Watch opens on a mic; speak an activity to start it.
claims.quote: Your Apple Watch opens on a microphone. Tap it, say what you’re doing

claims.detail: Log sets by voice on the watch.
claims.quote: Log sets by voice mid-workout.

claims.detail: Starting on phone starts watch workout automatically even if app closed.
claims.quote: Start a workout on your phone and your Apple Watch now starts the same workout automatically — even if the watch app was closed

claims.feature: Watch rest screen with heart rate
claims.detail: Rest ring countdown with HR and ±30s.
claims.quote:
The watch rest screen is redesigned: a ring counting down, your heart rate,
−30s / +30s in the corners.

claims.detail: Swipe on watch rest timer to see next set.
claims.quote: On the watch, swipe right on the rest timer to see what’s coming

claims.detail: Control music during rest on watch.
claims.quote: During a rest on the watch, swipe across to control your music.

claims.detail: Supersets alternate round by round on watch.
claims.quote: Supersets now alternate on your watch the way they do on your phone.

claims.detail: Mark warmup/failure/drop by voice on watch.
claims.quote: Voice on the watch can mark a set as warmup, failure, or drop

claims.detail: Start rest any time on watch.
claims.quote: Start a rest timer any time from the Apple Watch

claims.detail: Watch post-workout summary with HR line chart.
claims.quote: Apple Watch post-workout summary now shows a heart-rate line chart through your workout, matching the phone.

claims.detail: Friend workouts and competition invites delivered on the watch.
claims.quote: Friend workouts and competition invites land on your watch, ready to answer.

claims.detail: Splyt ring and streak complications on watch face.
claims.quote: Put your daily SPLYT ring right on your Apple Watch face.

claims.detail: Daily ring auto-updates as a watch face through a Photos album.
claims.quote: Splyt Ring watch face — your daily ring auto-updates as an Apple Watch face through a Photos album.

claims.detail: Watch asks for pool length in yards/meters.
claims.quote: Pool Swim on Apple Watch now asks for your pool length before starting

claims.detail: Watch follows phone accent color.
claims.quote: Watch app accent color now follows the phone

claims.detail: Elapsed clock shows centiseconds when wrist raised.
claims.quote: Apple Watch elapsed clock now ticks centiseconds (M:SS.CC) when your wrist is raised

claims.detail: Use the watch without a phone on the gym floor.
claims.quote: phones needed on the gym floor. The Watch does the lot.

claims.detail: Two-way sync for workouts, sleep, steps, weight.
claims.quote: Two-way sync for workouts, sleep, steps and weight. Your rings match your Watch.

claims.detail: Apple Fitness, Strava, Nike Run Club and GymKit workouts sync into history.
claims.quote: Workouts from Apple Fitness, Strava and gym treadmills land in your history automatically.

claims.detail: Sleep stages and nightly sleep score from Apple Health.
claims.quote: See your sleep stages and a nightly sleep score straight from Apple Health.

claims.detail: Add a night of sleep by hand, saved to Apple Health.
claims.quote: Add a night of sleep by hand — tap the “+” in your Sleep view to log when you went to bed and woke up.

claims.detail: Log weight and measurements synced with Apple Health.
claims.quote: Log body weight and measurements, kept in sync with Apple Health both ways.

claims.detail: Steps history chart with week/month/6-month/year.
claims.quote: A new Steps history chart in Stats, with Week, Month, 6-Month, and Year views.

claims.detail: Move/Exercise/Stand rings with custom goals, no Apple Fitness needed.
claims.quote: Your Move, Exercise and Stand rings in SPLYT, with goals you can set yourself.

claims.detail: Hourly Move/Exercise/Stand charts plus steps, distance, flights.
claims.quote: hourly Move/Exercise/Stand bar charts, plus Steps, Distance, and Flights Climbed.

claims.detail: Private progress photos with weekly reminders.
claims.quote: Progress Photos (Pro): keep private progress photos to see how you’re changing over time — and let Splyt remind you weekly

claims.detail: HR chart on summary with time in each zone.
claims.quote: Heart rate chart on the summary — a workout-window bar chart with a tap-through detail view that breaks down your time in each heart-rate zone.

claims.detail: Track daily habits with streaks and reminders.
claims.quote: Track any daily habit with streaks, reminders and weekly targets that fit real life.

claims.detail: Habits tick off from Apple Health (steps, sleep, bedtime, rings, activity).
claims.quote: A step goal, enough sleep, an earlier bedtime, waking up earlier, closing your rings, a specific activity — SPLYT already knows, so these tick themselves off.

claims.detail: Habits with N-per-week target or fixed number of weeks.
claims.quote: Habits can now have a weekly target (like 4× a week) or run for a set number of weeks

claims.detail: Reminders and private habits.
claims.quote: Pick the days or a number per week, add a reminder, or keep it private.

claims.detail: Each habit has its calendar, count, best streak.
claims.quote: Every habit keeps its own calendar, its count and its best streak.

claims.detail: One ring blending workout, habits and sleep/steps.
claims.quote: Three equal parts: your workout, your habits, and your sleep or steps.

claims.detail: Turn pillars off or set your own activity rule.
claims.quote: Your ring is actually yours — turn pillars off or set your own activity rule

claims.detail: Notification when all ring pillars complete.
claims.quote: You now get a “Splyt ring closed!” notification the moment you complete all three of your Splyt pillars for the day.

claims.detail: Nudge when one item away from a perfect day.
claims.quote: A new nudge gives you a heads-up when you're just one thing away from a perfect day

claims.detail: Volume breakdown by body part.
claims.quote: A new volume breakdown by body part on your Stats page shows where your training is going.

claims.detail: 0-21 daily exertion score with per-body-part breakdown.
claims.quote: A daily 0–21 effort score that shows which muscles drove your day.

claims.detail: Workout times chart with planned vs actual.
claims.quote: The same press-and-hold works on the Workout Times chart too

claims.detail: Workouts-per-week bar chart.
claims.quote: Workouts-per-week bar chart in the Stats tab shows your training consistency at a glance.

claims.detail: Lifted volume and cardio minutes over time.
claims.quote: watch your lifted volume and cardio minutes trend over time

claims.detail: Weight over ninety days.
claims.quote: Weight over ninety days, volume by week, and your personal records as they fall.

claims.detail: Workouts vs recovery chart with sleep stacking.

- CONFLICT: the CURRENT App Store description still advertises things later sources remove: "Pair Splyt to a treadmill, bike, rower, elliptical, or stair climber over Bluetooth", "food you can log in plain English" / "Log lifts, cardio, sleep, food...", and "Hands-free voice mode, with a lineup of natural voices and a vibe to match, from Calm to Drill Sergeant". Per instructions these are recorded under `removed`, not as claims. The App Store copy should be updated to match.
- Removal evidence strength: food logging has an explicit public removal line (build 374). Bluetooth pairing, voice vibes, hands-free voice chat and demo mode have NO explicit public "removed" statement: Bluetooth is implied by build 342 ("Splyt tracks straight from the watch") and build 326 ("record on Apple Fitness ... Splyt imports it"); vibes by build 342 ("a focused set of four natural-sounding voices"); hands-free voice chat only by its appearing under the roadmap's "Coming next" ("Talk to your coach"); demo mode has no public removal quote at all (the quote given is the original launch line) — removal is per caller instruction.
- Exercise library: "1,513 exercises" comes from the roadmap's "Under the hood" block (not the SHIPPED list); the older App Store note said "800+ exercises". Drop if only SHIPPED-section claims are allowed.
- Platform: requires iOS 17 per website (App Store lookup says minimumOsVersion 16.4); App Store lookup lists iPad devices (iosUniversal) but no public iPad feature claim was found. No Android or web app claimed.
- Pro-gated (not excluded, just noted): voice logging, auto rep counting, AI coach, progress photos (+AI analysis), AI support chat.
- Some changelog wording names the app ("Splyt AI", "Splyt ring"); feature names were neutralised.
- 'Group check-in challenges', 'PR spotlight', 'Community space' come from May 2026 entries; nothing later removes them and the roadmap SHIPPED list still includes "SPLYT Community".
